decisions.reason: The normalized geometric edge invariant fixes a standard convention, but the definition never assigns its three parameters to the three edge pairs and also omits the normal-path convention. Explicit edge labels and normal representatives now remove both ambiguities.

F3 explicitly cites the independent argument in supplier step 1.1 and its Remark, both of which prove total differentiability for continuous homeomorphisms with finite partials, without assuming quasiconformality. Supplier step 2.1 proves the orientation sign by a boundary homotopy. The area/Tonelli bound, Sobolev converse, ACL identification and rank-one exclusion meet those hypotheses.

The primitive in step 1.1 has the wrong sign, while the claimed integral A/2 is correct. Replacing it by -1/(2t^2) yields A(0-(-1/2))=A/2. Step 2.1 correctly bounds escaping length below by logarithmic height. The statement is unchanged.

The cited boundary-extension supplier explicitly calculates the distance formula, ball model, geodesic uniqueness and Mobius isometric extensions in its step 1.1. The assigned proof separately derives the sinh radial metric from the actual Jacobi and Cartan–Hadamard hypotheses, identifies PSL2(C) by Hermitian matrices, and proves discreteness and torsion-freeness of the deck group. F3 is supported by the cited argument.

The horocusp supplier proves discrete-subgroup closedness in L1, diagonal cyclicity in step 2.1, the parabolic centralizer computation in step 3.1, and the rank bound in step 4.1. These are the exact auxiliary claims used here. The small-matrix commutator estimate, finite-index prefix argument, elementary thin-component models, positive-volume packing and exclusion of rank-one cusps then establish the stated finite decomposition.

F1 attributes regularity to a definition that only fixes the model and shapes. F2 already proves all six angles are pi/3 at omega, so this is a nonfatal fact-attribution defect, repaired by limiting F1 to its definition and attributing regularity explicitly to F2. The six-region volume computation and convergent series retain the same conclusion.

The original metric definition imposed no compatibility at all with P, so it did not define a structure on the marked pared pair. The repair distinguishes a generic hyperbolic metric from a pared structure and requires injective discrete parabolic peripheral holonomy of the correct rank. Torus cusps must be embedded marked end neighborhoods; the annular/geodesic-boundary qualification is explicit. Yoshida Section 2, printed p.459, was consulted for the pared locus and annular cusp conventions.

The supplied closure definition explicitly distinguishes a raw topological image from the smooth-category closure. For finite elementary words it retains smooth endpoint-flat representatives without a choice assumption; K8 denotes that smooth oriented closure, not the raw diamond paths. F6 only names exterior/peripheral terminology: the diagram cutting in step 1.1 and the torus-link computation supply the complement and its peripheral end directly, without applying a product-tube theorem to a nonsmooth raw image. Face, edge and corner traces, both diagrams, and the regular-shape equations agree.

F2 explicitly cites the bound proved in the boundary-extension supplier, not only its Statement. Supplier steps 5.1–6.1 normalize an ideal triangle and bound points near all three sides in a compact set, giving the uniform center bound. Thus F and the realizing isometry are uniformly close as used in step 3.1. The Haar-mass calculation meets F3, the centralizer argument gives uniqueness, and the convex horoball tail argument supplies properness of the homotopy to any proper equivalence.

F1 defines only topological terms and has no choice premise; F2 assumes full AC, not an AC-omega branch. The repair states that exact F2 hypothesis, proves AC implies countable choice by restriction, and locates the inherited countable-choice use in the chosen tubular exterior definition. The nontrivial smooth-knot hypotheses still give both conclusions directly, and atoroidality/non-Seifertness are harmless extra hypotheses.
